Frequently Asked Questions (SaaS NDR & Churn Calculator)

What is the exact formula for Net Dollar Retention (NDR)?

Net Dollar Retention (NDR) measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from an existing customer cohort over a 12-month period. Formula: NDR = [(Starting ARR + Expansion ARR - Contraction ARR - Churned ARR) / Starting ARR] × 100. An NDR above 100% indicates net negative revenue churn.

How does Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) differ from NDR?

Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) measures revenue retention without crediting expansion or upsells. Formula: GRR = [(Starting ARR - Contraction ARR - Churned ARR) / Starting ARR] × 100. GRR can never exceed 100%. While top enterprise SaaS companies boast 120%–135% NDR, their GRR is typically 90%–95%.

What is a healthy SaaS Quick Ratio?

The SaaS Quick Ratio measures growth efficiency by comparing revenue additions against revenue losses: Quick Ratio = (New ARR + Expansion ARR) / (Contraction ARR + Churned ARR). A ratio greater than 4.0 indicates hyper-efficient compounding growth, 2.0 to 4.0 indicates solid growth, while below 2.0 indicates that customer churn is severely eroding acquisition efforts.
